title: Homogeneous maps, symbol estimates and completeness
scope: Symbols on open cones and equivariant bundles; continuous homogeneous pullback in four parameter regimes; submersions and proper maps; symbol topology, asymptotic summation, finite differences and weaker-order cutoffs; four solved examples.

mathematical_contents: Fréchet completeness follows directly from uniform derivative limits and the fundamental theorem.
Every homogeneous pullback case uses a higher-derivative count and finite-seminorm continuity.
Coordinate and equivariant-frame independence include the explicit homogeneous bundle weight.
Homogeneous submersions have explicit local sections and a continuous left inverse at all intrinsic orders.
Properness is equivalent to properness of the ray map and gives the stated normalized-support consequences.
Asymptotic summation is constructed with a diagonal cutoff choice and every derivative bound.
Finite differences recover differentiated asymptotics; the polynomial exponent is uniform in the partial-sum index.
Bounded-set topology equivalence and the all-orders extension principle follow from the finite-difference estimate and compact exhaustion.
Four complete examples show both sharp parameter restrictions, the nonproper support failure and the weaker-order cutoff limit.
component_terms: Programme exposition, proofs, solved examples and figure: CC0. Linked human sources retain their stated terms.
scope_boundary: The symbol estimates do not alone imply stationary phase, Fourier-integral composition, Sobolev mapping, involutivity or propagation at unrestricted derivative-loss parameters. Elementary external proofs are linked rather than reproduced.
